extracted.intended_audience: researchers and organizers interested in preprint peer review and open-science initiatives (including early-career researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for running a crowd-sourced public preprint review trial (workflow, participation, tools, and dissemination), illustrated by ASAPbio's cell-biology trial on Sciety. Aimed at groups organizing preprint review activities and researchers who might participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of preprint review
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprint review brings many benefits: valuable feedback for authors, further contextualization of the work for readers, and an opportunity for those who participate to hone reviewing skills and contribute to scientific discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these stated benefits as goals when designing review activities and in evaluating whether a trial or program is successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage participation from a diverse range of researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: ASAPbio is keen to experiment with new ways of encouraging participation from a diverse range of researchers, since participation in public preprint feedback is still relatively low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design recruitment/outreach to lower barriers to entry and actively invite diverse participants (career stage, institution, geography, subfield).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus trials on one specific discipline and set a short, reasonable time period
rubrics_metrics.description: The trial was focused on one specific discipline - cell biology - and a short period of time - three months - to keep the commitment by trial participants to a reasonable level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When piloting a crowd review model, limit scope by discipline and time to make participation manageable and to simplify evaluation of the experiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the workflow for contributing comments as simple as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: The organisers tried to keep the workflow for contributing comments on the preprints as simple as possible, running the trial using existing available tools to keep technical requirements to a minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer low-friction tools and minimal technical onboarding; avoid bespoke platforms unless necessary. Simplicity increases uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain authors' consent before including preprints in the trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Organisers contact the authors of the preprint for their consent to include the paper in the trial; if the authors agree, the preprint is circulated to the crowd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make author consent an explicit procedural requirement to respect author preferences and to facilitate later public posting of syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Hypothes.is for inline annotation during a defined short commenting window
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members are invited to comment on the preprint using Hypothes.is annotation during the following seven days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an established inline-annotation tool (Hypothes.is was used) and set a clear, short window (e.g., seven days) for concentrated commenting to encourage focused engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize comments into a single public TRiP review and post on bioRxiv and Sciety
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the commenting period, organisers synthesize all the comments received into a single review, which is posted publicly as a TRiP review on bioRxiv and on Sciety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear synthesis step that turns dispersed annotations into a coherent, citable public review; publish on recognized platforms for visibility and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit and enable early-career researchers as crowd members
rubrics_metrics.description: The call for participation attracted almost 100 researchers who signed up to be crowd members, the majority of whom are early career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target and support early-career researchers (who may particularly benefit from skill-building/opportunities) when recruiting crowd reviewers; keep sign-up open to expand participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulate preprints regularly (weekly) for feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Each week, the organisers circulate preprints for feedback and the group responds with public evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a regular cadence (e.g., weekly) for distributing papers to the crowd to sustain momentum and predictable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable collaborative interactions among crowd members (replies/endorsements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Crowd members can reply to each other’s comments for clarification or endorsement, which helps make the review feel like a team effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow and encourage threaded replies or endorsement mechanisms so contributors can clarify, build on, or converge around points, enhancing quality and coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target moderate contributor counts per synthesized review (example: 5–9 contributors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the reviews posted is the result of comments contributed by 5-9 crowd members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a manageable number of active contributors per preprint so the synthesis is tractable while still reflecting multiple perspectives; use the 5–9 range as an example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reviews publicly available to increase awareness, access and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The group’s public evaluations are made available on bioRxiv and Sciety; Sciety is focused on enabling efforts by creating technology that increases awareness of and access to outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish synthesized reviews on public platforms to maximize their utility for authors and readers and to increase discoverability and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate the experiment by surveying authors and crowd members and share lessons learned
rubrics_metrics.description: ASAPbio will be learning from this experiment by surveying preprint authors and the crowd members to learn more about their experience and will share what they learn after the trial is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include built-in evaluation (surveys/interviews) of participants and stakeholders and commit to sharing results to inform future iterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the Select Crowd model combining inline comments with full comprehensive reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The approach is based on the Select Crowd pioneered by Synlett, a model that allowed brief inline commenting on specific parts of the paper in addition to providing full comprehensive reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine fine-grained inline annotations with an overall synthesized review to capture both detailed and high-level evaluation; consider confidentiality implications if adapting from journal models to public preprint review.
